title: Rollout sprint-bridge and evaluation timeline for slow-path optimizations
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Context: We are optimizing the 'slow path' used when KV cache misses or long-context fallbacks occur. These slow-path improvements (kernel scheduling tweaks + reduced prefix rehydration) aim to reduce p95 token latency and lower unit cost under high variance workloads. This ticket defines the sprint-bridge (short cross-team deliverable spanning Product/Eng/Observability) and the evaluation milestones for a controlled rollout. Goal is to prove latency regressions do not occur for latency-sensitive routes and to measure cost delta at production traffic levels.
goals: Validate p95 generation latency improves on slow-path by >=15% at representative loads
Ensure overall endpoint p95 remains within 120ms for priority routes during canary
Measure per-token unit cost change and keep average increase below 8% (or demonstrate net savings from batching)
Ship rollout automation (traffic split + auto-fallback) and dashboarding for early detection
acceptance_criteria: Canary (0.5% -> 1% -> 5%) shows no P95 increase >5ms for priority routes over 24h windows
No increase in user-facing error rate > 0.05% attributable to the change during phased rollout
Telemetry shows KV cache miss tail latency reduced by >= 15% with 95% confidence
Runbook validated with on-call during 1st canary; rollback executed successfully in dry-run
Documentation updated: design doc, rollout checklist, and observability links are published
rollout_plan: Preflight (internal QA + synthetic traffic): complete by 2025-03-07
Canary phase 1: 0.5% traffic for 6 hours -> evaluate core metrics
Canary phase 2: 1% traffic for 24 hours -> broader SLO checks and error analysis
Canary phase 3: 5% traffic for 48 hours -> cost analysis and downstream service checks
Graduated ramp: 20% for 48 hours then 50% for 24 hours; final cutover when metrics stable
Automated fallback: if any gating metric breaches, traffic shifts to previous model variant and alerting page is triggered
telemetry_signals: user-perceived L7 latency on regional frontends
monitoring_plan: Dashboards: runtime/slow-path-optimizations (p95, p99, error-rate, token-cost) + canary-specific panels. Alerts: SRE alert if p95 increases more than 10ms vs baseline or error-rate delta > 0.03% in 15m. Weekly automated report for experiment owners for first 2 weeks. Instrumentation tags: experiment_id=PM-49512, cohort, variant_id. Include synthetic probes from three regions during canary windows.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Unobserved downstream retries causing hidden cost spike. Mitigation: add downstream retry margin to cost model and monitor retry_rate closely.
Risk: Region-specific degradation during ramp. Mitigation: region-aware canary throttles and synthetic probes from each region before ramp steps.
Risk: Rollout automation bug fails to revert traffic. Mitigation: manual rollback playbook and runbook-run verification prior to each phase
notes_for_reviews: PM asks reviewers to focus on gating thresholds (p95 delta tolerance and cost ceiling) and to validate that alert runbooks are actionable. SRE should confirm rollback path meets 2-minute recovery SLAs in staging. Observability to confirm metrics are tagged with experiment_id and cohort before canary start.
